title: Revenue Leakage Meaning: What People Actually Mean (and Confuse)
description: Revenue leakage meaning vs churn, shrinkage, and margin erosion — plain-language definitions for founders and operators.

faq.a: It means earned or almost-earned revenue is lost due to process failures — billing, funnel, or operations — rather than lack of market demand.

faq.q: Is revenue leakage the same as revenue shrinkage?
faq.a: Shrinkage often refers to inventory or retail loss. Revenue leakage usually describes funnel and billing gaps in digital and service businesses.

blocks.text: When people search revenue leakage meaning, they usually want a plain definition — not a finance textbook. Here it is: leakage is money slipping out of your business because a step in the journey failed, not because the market vanished.
Terms people confuse with revenue leakage

items: Churn: customers who leave — one source of leakage, not the whole picture
Margin erosion: often caused by discounts that never expire or scope creep
Leakage vs attrition: attrition is loss of customers; leakage includes never converting them at all
Revenue recognition errors: accounting timing — related but not identical

blocks.text: For a full framework across six leak categories, read [revenue leakage analysis](/blog/revenue-leakage-analysis).
